userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for caption focus area
userStories.notes: Seed story completed. Generated 11 stories (US-59-002 through US-59-012) covering: pre-flight format discovery, negative cache integration, format-specific error differentiation, FormatTimeoutPolicy integration, early termination on no-captions, auto-generated caption fallback, batch pre-flight deduplication, caption metrics dashboard, retry budget per-format tracking, caption stage transcription fallback coordination, and list-subs output caching.

userStories.title: Wire pre-flight list-subs check into format fallback loop
acceptanceCriteria: _fetch_subtitle() calls list_available_languages() before iterating formats when no cached language data exists for the video
If list_available_languages() returns empty list, _fetch_subtitle() raises CaptionUnavailableError immediately without trying any format
If list_available_languages() returns languages but none match the requested language, _fetch_subtitle() raises CaptionUnavailableError with descriptive message listing available languages
Pre-flight check is skipped when caption cache already has a valid entry for the video (avoids redundant yt-dlp call)
Unit test verifies that a video with no captions triggers exactly 1 yt-dlp invocation (list-subs) instead of 3+ format attempts
userStories.notes: All 5 criteria verified. Implementation at src/caption_fetcher.py:4041-4075 (pre-flight check with cache), tests at tests/test_caption_preflight.py (7 tests, all passing).

userStories.title: Integrate negative cache (store_unavailable) into caption fetcher
acceptanceCriteria: When _fetch_subtitle() determines no captions exist (via pre-flight or exhausted formats), it calls cache.store_unavailable(video_id, language) before raising CaptionUnavailableError
At the start of fetch_captions() or fetch_captions_with_retry(), cache.is_caption_unavailable(video_id, language) is checked and returns early if True
Negative cache entries use the existing staleness policy (strict/warn/skip modes) from CaptionCache
Unit test verifies that a second fetch attempt for a known-unavailable video hits the negative cache and makes zero yt-dlp subprocess calls
Negative cache integration works with both single-video and batch fetch paths
userStories.notes: All 5 criteria verified. Added caption_cache param to CaptionFetcher.__init__, negative cache check at start of fetch_captions(), store_unavailable() call before raising CaptionUnavailableError. Added store_unavailable() and is_caption_unavailable() methods to CaptionCache in caption_fetcher.py with staleness policy support (strict/warn/skip). Wired caption_cache in caption_stage.py and iterative_match.py. Tests: 10 tests in tests/test_negative_cache.py, all 419 existing caption tests pass.

userStories.title: Differentiate 'format unavailable' from 'no captions at all' in error handling
acceptanceCriteria: _fetch_subtitle_with_format() at line 4114 distinguishes between 'Requested format is not available' (format-specific) and 'no subtitles'/'subtitles are disabled' (video-level) in stderr parsing
When stderr contains 'Requested format is not available', a new CaptionFormatUnavailableError is raised (subclass of CaptionFetchError) instead of generic CaptionFetchError
When _fetch_subtitle() catches CaptionUnavailableError from any format attempt, it breaks the loop immediately instead of trying remaining formats (no captions means no captions in any format)
Unit test verifies that 'Requested format is not available' error on json3 still tries vtt/srt, while 'no subtitles' error on json3 stops immediately
Existing error categorization in src/caption/error_handling.py categorize_caption_error() handles the new error type correctly
userStories.notes: Implemented US-59-004: Added CaptionFormatUnavailableError (subclass of CaptionFetchError) in exceptions.py. Updated _fetch_subtitle_with_format() to detect 'requested format is not available' in stderr and raise format-specific error. Changed _fetch_subtitle() loop to re-raise CaptionUnavailableError (breaking loop) while continuing on CaptionFormatUnavailableError. Added FORMAT_UNAVAILABLE to CaptionErrorCategory enum with retry budget 0. Updated categorize_caption_error() for both instance-based and string-based detection. 21 tests pass.

userStories.title: Integrate FormatTimeoutPolicy into _fetch_subtitle_with_format
acceptanceCriteria: _fetch_subtitle_with_format() uses FormatTimeoutPolicy.get_timeout(subtitle_format, fallback_level) instead of the flat self._timeout for the subprocess.run timeout parameter
fallback_level is derived from the format's position in the current preference order (0 for first format, 1 for second, etc.)
CaptionFetcher.__init__() instantiates FormatTimeoutPolicy with configurable base timeouts from caption_first config section
Unit test verifies that json3 gets a longer timeout (45s) than vtt/srt (25s) as defined in FormatTimeoutPolicy defaults
Unit test verifies that the third format attempt gets a reduced timeout (0.8x multiplier per fallback_level)
userStories.notes: Implemented US-59-005: Integrated FormatTimeoutPolicy into CaptionFetcher. _fetch_subtitle_with_format() now uses format-specific timeouts (json3=45s, srv3=30s, vtt/srt=25s) with 0.8x progressive fallback reduction. Added format_timeouts config field to CaptionFirstConfig for overrides. 12 unit tests in tests/test_format_timeout_policy_integration.py verify defaults, fallback reduction, and CaptionFetcher integration.

userStories.title: Add early termination in batch fetch when all errors are 'no captions'
acceptanceCriteria: fetch_captions_batch() tracks a counter of consecutive CaptionUnavailableError results across the batch
When 80% or more of the last 10 videos return CaptionUnavailableError, a warning is logged suggesting the source may not have captions
Early termination does NOT abort the batch — it logs the warning and continues, but switches remaining videos to 'pre-flight only' mode (list-subs check, skip format attempts if no subs found)
CaptionMetrics records the unavailable_count and unavailable_rate in the batch summary
Unit test verifies that a batch of 20 videos where first 10 all lack captions triggers the warning and the remaining 10 use pre-flight-only mode
userStories.notes: Implemented US-59-006: Added unavailable pattern detection to BatchProcessor. Rolling window of last 10 results tracks CaptionUnavailableError rate. When 80%+ are unavailable, logs warning and switches remaining videos to preflight-only mode (has_captions check before full fetch). CaptionMetrics records unavailable_count and unavailable_rate in summary/to_dict/from_dict. 7 unit tests in TestBatchProcessorUnavailableDetection verify threshold detection, preflight switching, metrics tracking, and serialization. All 34 batch processor tests + 91 related tests pass.

userStories.title: Add auto-generated caption fallback in _fetch_subtitle
acceptanceCriteria: When _fetch_subtitle() fails to find manual captions (auto_generated=False), it retries with auto_generated=True before raising CaptionUnavailableError
The auto-generated fallback only triggers when the error is caption unavailability (not rate limits, timeouts, or network errors)
Auto-generated fallback respects the existing allow_auto_generated config flag (default True) and skips if False
CaptionResult.is_auto_generated is set to True when auto-generated fallback is used, preserving quality metadata
Unit test verifies that a video with only auto-generated captions returns a CaptionResult with is_auto_generated=True after manual caption attempt fails
userStories.notes: Tier: enhancement. _fetch_subtitle() at src/caption_fetcher.py:4005 receives auto_generated as a parameter but the caller chain doesn't implement a manual-then-auto fallback. The method tries all formats with the given auto_generated value, then gives up. The --write-auto-subs flag is already used at line 4081 when auto_generated=True. fetch_captions_auto_language() at line 2780 handles language fallback but not manual-to-auto fallback. determine_caption_quality() at line 71 already scores auto-generated lower. Key files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines 4005-4056 _fetch_subtitle, line 4081 sub_flag, line 2780 fetch_captions_auto_language).

userStories.title: Deduplicate list-subs calls for same-channel videos in batch fetch
acceptanceCriteria: fetch_captions_batch() extracts channel ID from video_search_results metadata when available
A channel_caption_availability dict caches the list-subs result (available languages) per channel_id
When a video's channel already has a cached list-subs result showing no captions in the requested language, the video is marked unavailable without making a yt-dlp call
The channel cache is per-batch (not persisted) and only used as a heuristic — individual videos can still override if the channel cache shows 'unavailable' but video-specific data hasn't been checked
Unit test verifies that 5 videos from the same channel result in at most 2 list-subs calls (first video + one retry after unavailable)
userStories.notes: Tier: optimization. fetch_captions_batch() at src/caption_fetcher.py:3230 processes videos in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor. Channel-based prioritization already exists (US-009 Sprint 7) at lines 3360-3372 tracking channel_success_rates. Video metadata from video_search_results includes channel_id in most cases. The channel pattern tracking in CaptionMetrics (channel_patterns dict at ~line 6710) could be extended. Key files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines 3230-3922 fetch_captions_batch, lines 3360-3372 channel prioritization, lines 6710+ CaptionMetrics.channel_patterns).

userStories.title: Add caption fetch performance summary to CaptionMetrics
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionMetrics gains a record_format_attempt(video_id, format_name, success, elapsed_seconds) method that tracks per-format attempt counts and durations

CaptionMetrics gains a get_performance_summary() method returning a dict with: total_subprocess_calls, total_subprocess_seconds, avg_seconds_per_call, calls_saved_by_preflight, calls_saved_by_negative_cache
The performance summary is included in the existing generate_summary_report() output at line ~8047
_fetch_subtitle_with_format() calls record_format_attempt() after each subprocess invocation
Unit test verifies that performance summary accurately reflects the number of subprocess calls and time spent
userStories.notes: Tier: observability. CaptionMetrics at src/caption_fetcher.py:6710 already tracks format_success_counts and extensive batch statistics, but doesn't track per-format attempt counts (only successes) or subprocess call timing. The generate_summary_report() method at line ~8047 outputs format stats but not performance/efficiency data. Adding this enables measuring the impact of pre-flight checks and negative caching from US-59-002 and US-59-003. Key files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines 6710-7000 CaptionMetrics class, lines 8047-8130 generate_summary_report, line 4104 subprocess.run call in _fetch_subtitle_with_format).

userStories.title: Track retry budget consumption per subtitle format
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionRetryBudget gains a format_attempts dict tracking attempts per subtitle format (json3, vtt, srt)
record_attempt() accepts an optional format parameter and increments the format-specific counter
budget_exhausted() can optionally check per-format exhaustion (e.g., stop trying json3 after N consecutive failures across different videos)
to_dict() and from_dict() serialize/deserialize the format_attempts field for checkpoint persistence
Unit test verifies that per-format tracking correctly accumulates across multiple videos and survives checkpoint round-trip
userStories.notes: Tier: enhancement. CaptionRetryBudget at src/caption/retry_budget.py:73 tracks global attempts, per-video attempts (attempts_per_video_id at line 147), and error categories (error_counts), but not per-format attempts. This means the budget can't detect that e.g. json3 is consistently failing across all videos (suggesting a yt-dlp or YouTube API issue with that format). Adding per-format tracking enables smarter format skipping when a format is systematically broken. Key files: src/caption/retry_budget.py (lines 73-350, especially record_attempt at 208, budget_exhausted at 341, to_dict/from_dict).

userStories.title: Coordinate caption stage with transcription fallback on batch-wide unavailability
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionStage.run() checks the batch result summary after fetch_captions_batch() completes and logs how many videos had captions vs how many fell back to unavailable
When more than 50% of videos in the batch have no captions, CaptionStage sets a state flag (state.caption_batch_low_yield = True) that downstream stages can read
The state flag is persisted in checkpoint.json so --resume preserves it
DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS stage reads caption_batch_low_yield and logs a warning that many videos will need transcription after download
Unit test verifies that state.caption_batch_low_yield is set when 6 out of 10 videos return no captions
userStories.notes: Tier: enhancement. CaptionStage at src/stages/caption_stage.py:138 runs the batch and stores results in state.text_metadata and state.caption_results, but doesn't summarize batch-wide caption availability for downstream stages. Currently, the pipeline discovers missing captions only during DOWNLOAD_SEGMENTS when it tries to use them. The state object (src/state.py) already supports arbitrary attributes. Checkpoint persistence is handled by src/checkpoint.py. Key files: src/stages/caption_stage.py (line 138 run method), src/state.py, src/stages/download_segments.py, src/checkpoint.py.

userStories.title: Cache list-subs output to avoid redundant pre-flight calls on resume
acceptanceCriteria: list_available_languages() checks a cache before making the yt-dlp --list-subs subprocess call
The cache key is video_id and the cached value includes the list of AvailableLanguage objects and a timestamp
Cache entries expire after a configurable TTL (default 1 hour) since subtitle availability can change
The cache is stored in the existing .cache/ directory structure (not in-memory only) so it persists across --resume runs
Unit test verifies that calling list_available_languages() twice for the same video within the TTL results in exactly 1 subprocess call
userStories.notes: Tier: optimization. list_available_languages() at src/caption_fetcher.py:2440 always makes a yt-dlp --list-subs call with no caching. If US-59-002 wires this into the fetch path, every video will incur an extra subprocess call (~10s) unless results are cached. The existing CaptionCache at src/caption/cache.py handles TTL-based caching for caption content but not for availability metadata. A lightweight addition to CaptionCache or a separate dict in CaptionFetcher would work. Key files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines 2440-2483 list_available_languages), src/caption/cache.py (base cache class with TTL support).
